text: # Lane 9 — above the plateau: what the ≥0.94 band is doing
T047 round-3 research note, 2026-09-02.
Read-only lane;
no GPU, no submission.
Written incrementally as evidence landed.
Question. Rounds 1 and 2 dissected the 0.936 shared notebook (lane 5) and the 0.924 public single model (lane 7).
Nobody had looked above the plateau.
As of lane 0's 2026-09-01 snapshot, 84 teams sat at ≥0.94 and 3 at ≥0.95 while we sat at 0.926.
What is that band doing that the plateau is not, and is any of it verifiable?
Verdict, stated up front. The lane came back positive, and its main result is a falsification.

The hypothesis the brief asked me to try to kill — that the whole ≥0.94 band is the plateau notebook plus submission-count-driven public overfitting — does not survive contact with the leaderboard's own submission counts. There is a control group of 86 teams that spent the same or larger submission budget as the median ≥0.94 team and stayed pinned at 0.936.
Budget is not what separates the band from the plateau.
Method is.
Details in §2.
Evidence marks. READ = quoted from a primary page, thread or file.
MEASURED = computed by me, command given.
INFERRED = an estimate with the model stated.
No number below is unmarked.
Method and sources
- Leaderboard: kaggle competitions leaderboard rsna-knee-abnormality-detection --download, run 2026-09-02T15:49 local. The file Kaggle served is stamped 2026-09-02T10:19:50Z and holds 2,889 teams.

- The download carries four fields lane 0 did not use: SubmissionCount, LastSubmissionDate, TeamMemberUserNames, TeamId.

This is the single most useful thing in the lane.

Full command list in appendix A.

### 1.1 There is no new plateau.
The 0.936 spike is still the only one.
This was the brief's first question and it has a clean answer.
Histogram at 0.001 resolution (MEASURED, outputs/t047/lb_analysis.py):
score
teams
score
teams

461 teams sit at exactly 0.936 — 16.0% of the entire board. Above it, 165 teams spread over 15 distinct score values with no bin exceeding 40, and the largest of those (0.937, n=40) is the plateau's own shoulder.
A spike-ratio test (bin ÷ its larger neighbour, MEASURED) makes the point numerically: every bin from 0.937 to 0.952 scores between 0.00 and 3.00, i.e. it is indistinguishable from its neighbours.
0.936 scores 6.78. One mode, not two.
Conclusion (MEASURED). No newer shared notebook has been published at 0.94x since round 1.
The ≥0.94 band is a smooth distribution, which by the brief's own decision rule means independent work, not a shared artifact.
Anyone hoping to find a 0.945 notebook to fork will not find one, and §4 confirms that directly by looking.

the plateau grew, the top did not
Lane 0's 2026-09-01T18:44Z counts against mine at 2026-09-02T10:19Z (MEASURED against READ):

The top is close to static;
the growth is at the plateau, which is what a shared notebook accumulating new forkers looks like.
Rank 1 is unchanged at 0.952 and Brandon Low's last submission was 2026-08-28 — he has been on top for five days without submitting, and none of the high-budget teams below him has closed 0.006.
That is worth holding onto for §2.
### 1.3 The band is 88 solo practitioners, not merged super-teams
Team sizes at ≥0.94 (MEASURED): 79 of 88 are one-person teams, 7 are pairs, one is a 3 and one is a 4.
Board-wide the figure is 2,687 solo of 2,889.
There is no merger wave at the top, and no evidence that the band is what you get by pooling people.
CloseAI (rank 2, 0.950, devansh26,liaoyixu) is the only pair in the top ten.
The falsification: the band is not bought with submissions
The brief's hypothesis, restated: lane 3 measured that ~200 submissions on structurally distinct candidates, keeping the best public score, manufactures +0.012 of public gain worth zero privately.
The plateau-to-rank-20 distance is +0.010.
Arithmetically consistent.
So — is the whole band public overfit?
No. Three measurements, in increasing order of force.
### 2.1 Submission count does track band membership — this part is true
MEASURED, outputs/t047/subs_analysis.py:
band
teams
median subs
mean
max
min
Above-plateau median is 34 submissions against the plateau's 10 — a 3.4× gap.
Taken alone this looks like the fitting story confirmed.
### 2.2 But within the band, more submissions buys nothing
If selection-on-public-score were producing the band's ordering, score should rise with submission count inside the band.
It does not (MEASURED, discrim.py, n=125 teams at ≥0.9375):
quartile by submissions
teams
median subs
median score
max score
Q1 fewest
Q4 most
A flat line from 16 submissions to 69.
Spearman ρ = 0.161, permutation p = 0.077 (20,000 permutations, seed 0) — not significant, and the effect size is negligible regardless.
Quadrupling your submission budget inside the band moves your median score by zero.
### 2.3 The control group: 86 teams spent the budget and did not move
This is the decisive measurement.
Within the plateau band (0.9355–0.9375, 501 teams, 8,366 submissions spent collectively):
- 461 of 501 are at exactly 0.936 (MEASURED).
- 86 of those teams have ≥30 submissions each, median 41, maximum 119.
- The complete set of distinct scores achieved by those 86 high-budget teams is {0.936, 0.937} (MEASURED, discrim.py).
Read that against §2.1.
The median team at ≥0.940 spent 36 submissions;
the median team at ≥0.9375 spent 34.
The control group's median is 41 — higher than either. Eighty-six teams outspent the typical band member and are still on the plateau.

Same budget, opposite outcome. Submission count is therefore not sufficient to reach the band, and the fitting story — which needs budget to be the active ingredient — cannot explain the 88 teams above 0.94.
The mechanism behind the control group is visible in the same number: a population sitting at exactly one value has zero variance in its submissions.
Those teams are re-running the same inference graph (nested configs, LB sd ≈ 0.0003 per our instrument table), not sampling structurally distinct candidates.
An order statistic of a zero-variance population is that same point.
So the plateau population cannot be the parent distribution whose upper tail is the ≥0.94 band.

Under the expected-maximum model E[max of N draws] ≈ sd·√(2·ln N) (INFERRED, model stated), 7 submissions buys +0.0057 at the nested-config sd of 0.0028 and +0.0143 at the structurally-distinct sd of 0.0070.
Tiago Mazzutti is +0.014 above the plateau on 7 submissions.

That sits at the very edge of the most generous version of the model, and the generous version requires all seven submissions to have been structurally distinct systems — which is method work, not fitting.
Rank 4 on seven submissions is not a lucky draw.
### 2.5 Verdict on the two worlds
The band is method, not fitting. More precisely, and stated with the hedging the evidence actually supports:
- Reaching ≥0.94 requires something structurally different from the plateau notebook. 86 control teams with heavy budgets prove budget alone will not do it (§2.3).
- The ordering inside the band is not bought with submissions either (§2.2), so even the within-band spread is not obviously fitting.
- What submissions do correlate with is being the kind of team that iterates on method — 34 versus 10 is a proxy for effort, not a causal lever.

- This does not mean the band's scores are privately safe. Lane 3's winner's-curse result still applies to any individual team's public-vs-private delta, and the 0.936→0.946 distance is still partly inflated.
The claim I am falsifying is narrower and it is the one that mattered strategically: chasing the band is not worthless, because the band is not an artefact of submission spending.

Strategic consequence. The brief said this finding "changes our strategy completely." It does, in the opposite direction to the one that was flagged as the risk: there is real, reachable skill above the plateau, and we are 0.010 below the plateau itself.
The gap to close is a method gap.
The band is dark, and its most-upvoted rivals are stuck

What the ≥0.94 band actually says it does
Round 1 never read the forum and lane 7 read four topics.
I swept all five pages of kaggle competitions topics list — 94 topics — and read the method threads.
The band talks, and several of the talkers are identifiable on the leaderboard.
A note on evidence class. None of these is ID-anchored (no submission ID is named).

But they are better than bare assertions: I matched each poster's display name to a leaderboard TeamName (MEASURED, outputs/t047/forum_xref.py), and in every case below the claimed score is at or below that team's verified public score.
I mark these LB-corroborated: the identity is verified and the claim is not inflated relative to a number Kaggle publishes.
That is weaker than ID-anchored and stronger than author-asserted.
### 4.1 The headline: the band is smaller and lower-resolution, not bigger
READ, topic 735304 "Best single-model score" (roy214, 37 comments, 21 votes) — the single most valuable thread on the forum:
> Tucker Arrants (2026-08-16): "Single model 0.934 @ 224px
> Update: 0.942 with some tweaks, still @ 224px"
> …asked "Is this a single fold, or N-fold ensemble?" he replies: "5 fold ensemble"
Tucker Arrants is rank 15, 0.947, 31 submissions (MEASURED).
LB-corroborated.
> Scott Willis (2026-08-20): "I'm at 0.938 with a single model, single fold.
> I'm also pretty new to all of this…"
> and (2026-08-22): "I just tried to start with as small of a model as possible.
> My whole goal was to start aiming for the efficiency LB and then go up from there."
Scott Willis is rank 7 on the main LB at 0.948 and rank 1 on the efficiency LB (MEASURED;
efficiency rank from lane 0).
LB-corroborated.
> Yann Majewski (2026-09-01): "0.936lb, single fold, small resnet model, 224x224"
Rank 251, 0.936, 17 submissions — his claim exactly equals his verified score.
> Tom Aindow (2026-08-15): "Single model 0.915, DinoV2 based.

> top results are ensembles, look at the efficiency lb, you can see many high

Rank 27, 0.945, 40 submissions.

LLM output labels only"
Not matchable to a TeamName;
0.926 @ 336px is exactly our position.
This is the answer to the lane's question. A single fold of a small ResNet at 224 px reaches the plateau.
A 5-fold of one model at 224 px reaches 0.942, i.e. rank ~50.
Meanwhile the 0.936 plateau notebook is 35 checkpoints across 4 architecture families at 336–384 px (lane 5 §2), and its own author sits at 0.936 with 52 submissions.
The band is not out-ensembling the plateau.
It is out-modelling it with less. Ensemble breadth is what the plateau has and the band does not need.
This contradicts lane 5 §1.3's reading that "the gap to 0.936 is in the ensemble breadth and the input representation" — the breadth half of that does not survive the forum evidence.
The input representation half survives;
the resolution direction in it does not.

The rank-15 team's teacher is at ~0.89 by their own statement.

We are not behind on labels, and the highest-placed team who has discussed it says labels are not the lever. This independently corroborates our ±0.036 gold-58 posture and argues against spending round-3 effort on the target side.

Corroborating, READ topic 735826 (Oscar Yáñez Feijóo, 11 comments), Tucker Arrants: "If your image model is not beating the label extractor 'teacher'…" and tennogh (rank 60, 0.941): "the reports just don't contain the information and clever 'fixes' end up overfitting to the 58 set."
### 4.3 Two things in the band that no prior lane has looked at
- Pillar-0 — fabotelli/pillar-0-knee-fine-tune-loader-demo, by the rank-88 team at 0.940, plus forum topic 738036 "Has anyone looked at Pillar-0?".
Absent from lanes 5, 6 and 7.
A medical-imaging foundation model used as an encoder by a team above the plateau.
- Resolution going down, not up. Lane 2 studied "encoder scaling" and lane 5 recommended 336–384 px.
Two LB-corroborated band members are at 224 px.
We are at 320 px.
Nobody has tested the downward direction here, and it is the cheapest possible experiment.

### 4.5 There is no metadata shortcut (someone checked properly)
READ, topic 733517 (Oleksii Zhukov, 17 votes), a pre-registered two-probe test:
> "DICOM metadata alone reaches 0.6515 macro AUC under random folds but only
> 0.598 across unseen scanners.
Safe to say no meaningful shortcuts found.
> Leaderboard scores seem to reflect image reading."
265 distinct scanner fingerprints;
the 0.053 random-vs-grouped gap is site memorisation that does not transfer.
Closes off a whole class of speculation at zero cost to us, and independently establishes that scanner-grouped folds and random folds differ by ~0.05 on metadata alone.
The single most actionable thing in the band: inference-time window count

### 5.1 The window-count curve

"0.02" — garbled in the original, almost certainly 0.92x

LB-corroborated — it is this team's verified public score

+0.010 of public LB from 42 → 94 windows per study, on one T4, from a single un-blended model, at zero additional training GPU. The author states plainly that the 9 h cap is consumed by window count, not model count.
### 5.2 Why this is the finding that matters for us
Our deployed kernel uses a bracketed 1.5–4.4 h of the 9 h cap (T047 lane 11 brief) with 22 members of one recipe.
This team spends the full 9 h on one model and 94 windows, and lands +0.014 above us.

The axis they are spending on is the one we are not spending on at all, and it is the only axis available to us that costs no local GPU and no training — which under the one-fold-then-cool-down ruling is the binding constraint on everything else.

INFERRED, model stated: if the 42→94 slope (+0.010 per ~2.2× windows) held for our recipe, and it may not because our members are already averaging across 22 checkpoints which captures some of the same variance, then moving from our current window budget into the unused ~5 h is a candidate for the largest zero-training-GPU gain identified in three rounds of research.
This is not a result;
it is a lever with a mechanism and a public data point. It belongs to lane 11 and should be routed there, not adopted here (T047 rule 3).

Instrument. The 869-study held-out corpus ρ (paired band ±0.0102) can measure whether window count changes our own predictions at all, at zero submissions — if predictions do not move, the lever is dead before it costs anything.
The OOF-AUC-vs-Sonnet instrument on 4,349 studies (±0.0019) is the tightest available and is the right gate.
Public LB would resolve it at sd 0.0028–0.0070 between structurally distinct configs, but we have 0 submissions, so it cannot.
Pre-registered rule to attach: window count is adopted only if OOF-AUC moves by more than +0.0019, measured before any submission is contemplated.
### 5.3 The counter-evidence, stated fairly
The same team says: "its around 9 hours for the full test set." That is at the rule limit with no margin.
Lane 0 READ the cap as "GPU Notebook ≤ 9 hours run-time".
A rerun that lands at 9 h is a submission that can fail.
Any version of this lever for us must be budgeted well inside the cap, which costs some of the gain.
It also makes them ineligible in practice for the efficiency track — they say so: "Just havent selected one of those for the efficiency side."

### 6.2 Ensemble breadth is not the discriminator either

- Scott Willis, rank 7 (0.948), efficiency rank 1: "I'm at 0.938 with a single model, single fold" and later "I did break down and submit a 5 fold ensemble though, so my current 0.947 is no longer a single fold." One model, one fold, 0.938 — above the plateau.
- Dread Development, rank 78: "no fold ensembling in it" (§5).
- Tom Aindow, rank 27: "Highly doubt the top results are ensembles, look at the efficiency lb… they're not running 20 different models.
Public notebooks just ensemble early on to try and get a high leaderboard score and exposure/kudos.
Waste of time IMO."
We run 22 members.
The plateau runs ~35 checkpoints across 4 arms and its author is stuck at 0.936 on 52 submissions.
Nothing above the plateau is being bought with member count, and the two populations that ensemble hardest are exactly the two that are stuck.
### 6.3 Labels are saturated, and the band says so with numbers
The strongest statement in the whole forum, READ, Tucker Arrants (rank 15, 0.947), 2026-08-31:
> "My CV is around 0.87 - 0.9 depending on the generated labels used, all
> leading to the same ~0.94 leaderboard score."
A 0.03 swing in teacher quality producing zero LB movement is a direct measurement that the target side is not binding at 0.94.
He adds:
> "Spent the last week or so getting 'better' labels and none of it translated to
> the LB.
Single prompt LLM extraction has not been beaten, outside of noise, by
> any more sophisticated extraction procedures that I have tried."
> "My best current LB model is from my first pass at extraction, with thousands of
> verified extraction failures.
I correct them, no change in LB. Image model
> 'student' seems to consistently outperform the label extractor 'teacher'."
And on the mechanism, which is the same one lane 4 found:
> "the reports genuinely do not contain the information required to generate the
> corresponding label … The radiologist writing the report either missed or simply
> did not care to report that particular label."
Our teacher reads gold at 0.8976;
his is "maybe 0.89". Two independent teams above us report the label lever exhausted.
This is strong external support for not spending round 3 on the target side, and it bears directly on lane 12's question.
### 6.4 Capacity is not binding either
READ, topic 735154 (stevenleehans, rank 735, 0.932, 11 votes) — a pre-registered null with a noise floor stated:
> "Swapping DINOv2-Small → DINOv2-Base (22M → 87M params, 3.9× the compute per
> step) moved our CV by +0.0011 against a measured noise floor of 0.0020.
> null. Only 5 of 12 labels moved in Base's favour… Capacity is not what's
> binding here."
He also reports the corpus compresses to 11.12 GiB (4,407 × 6 slots × 9 slices × 224², uint8) and that decode was "55 minutes per run, which was 72% of a single fold".
Corroborates lane 2's encoder-scaling finding from an independent team, and the transferable warning is his own: "a checkpoint carries its own preprocessing contract.
Swapping encoder weights without swapping the normalisation constants is a silent handicap that produces a plausible, wrong result."
### 6.5 A team at exactly our score, describing exactly our problem
READ, topic 735304, Berat Kirbiyik (not matchable on the LB):
> "we're stuck at 0.924 and every architectural lever we've tried has come back
> inside noise: larger backbone, cross-slot attention, top-k pooling, EMA, mixup,
> longer schedules, slice-count sweeps.
Seven ablations, all within 0.008 of
> each other. That pattern usually means the ceiling is upstream of the model."

He also reports "we got a CoAtNet-384 run down from 65 minutes to 17 by pipelining preprocessing against GPU." Independent confirmation that the 0.92x tier's architecture-side levers are exhausted — which is where we are.
### 6.6 The dissenting voice, recorded
Not everything supports §2.
Mattia Angeli (rank 231, 0.936, 96 submissions), topic 736268, 2026-08-20:
> "It's currently a race to overfit the public leaderboard, 0.001 at a time 😅"
And Scott Willis (rank 7, 0.948) on his own score:
> "I'm not too confident my score is going to hold on the private LB, though.
> Should be interesting to see."

I record these because they are the strongest statements for the hypothesis §2 rejects, and because the rank-7 team's own doubt about its private score is the appropriate caveat on everything above. §2 shows the band is not reachable by submission spending;
it does not show the band's public margins are private margins.

## Decision rules — fixed in advance
This task spends no GPU and no submissions, so its rules govern what it is allowed to claim, not what it may spend.
Every claim carries an evidence mark — READ, MEASURED, REPRODUCED or INFERRED — as rounds 1 and 2 required.
An unmarked number is a defect.
A lever enters the synthesis's ranked table only with an instrument named: which measurement would resolve it, at what band.
A lever with no instrument is recorded as not resolvable here and ranked last, never dropped silently.
Nothing is adopted by this task. Round 3 produces registered tasks with bands, not configuration changes.
A round-3 lane that finds nothing says so. A null lane is a result and is written up as one.
Four lanes returning four levers would be evidence of motivated reasoning, not of a productive round.
Prohibitions bind: no naive horizontal flip, no rule-constant tuning, no new LLM labeling pass, no GPU while T007 holds the card, no submission.
